skill.name: route-tester
skill.description: Test authenticated API routes in a local project with cookie-based JWT authentication, mock authentication, curl examples, and database verification steps.
skill.summary: Guides local testing of authenticated routes with JWT cookies, mock auth, route prefixes, and response checks.
skill.author: diet103

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-only, but it directs users to run local route-testing commands and modify authentication-related environment settings. Most localhost URL and Markdown backtick detections are false positives, while mock authentication guidance and hardcoded credentials are real risks if reused outside isolated development.

remediation.issue: Mock authentication can bypass real access controls.
remediation.suggestion: State that mock auth must be limited to disposable local environments, and include a rollback check that removes MOCK_AUTH before deployment.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded credentials appear in reusable documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Replace testuser, testpassword, and database root password examples with placeholders and environment-specific secret references.

remediation.issue: Command examples can affect local services and databases.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings to confirm the target environment before running node, curl, Docker, MySQL, or pm2 commands.

remediation.issue: The skill contains project-specific absolute paths and ports.
remediation.suggestion: Convert absolute paths and service URLs into configurable placeholders for each project.

semantic_findings.title: Mock Authentication Bypass Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to enable MOCK_AUTH and send mock user and role headers, including admin roles. This can bypass real authentication if copied into a shared or production-like environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly documents mock auth environment variables and headers with admin roles. It states development-only intent, but the instructions can materially weaken authentication if misapplied.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded Test Credentials and Database Password

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credentials are visible in the documented workflow, including a MySQL root password in a runnable command. They appear intended for local testing, but they remain sensitive defaults.

content.value_statement: Authenticated route testing can fail when tokens, cookies, and route prefixes are unclear. This skill gives repeatable local patterns for API checks, mock auth, and response validation.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to test cookie-authenticated routes with a helper script.
Shows curl patterns for POST requests, uploads, and protected endpoints.
Documents mock authentication settings for development and test environments.
Provides service port and route prefix guidance for local APIs.
Lists database checks for confirming route side effects.
limitations: The examples are specific to one project structure and local service ports.
It depends on existing scripts, middleware, and service configuration.
It does not provide an automated test runner or assertions.
Mock authentication guidance must not be used in production environments.

use_cases.title: Validate a New Endpoint
use_cases.description: Test a new authenticated route with expected request data and inspect the response.

use_cases.title: Debug Authorization Failures
use_cases.description: Compare token, cookie, role, and route prefix settings during local failure investigation.

use_cases.title: Confirm Workflow Side Effects
use_cases.description: Run route checks and verify expected database records after workflow actions.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Test Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the route-tester skill to help me test this local authenticated GET route: [route]. Identify the service port and command pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Test a POST Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the route-tester skill to create a local authenticated POST test for [route] with this request body: [body].

prompt_templates.title: Debug a 401 or 403
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the route-tester skill to debug why [route] returns [status]. Check cookie format, roles, route prefix, and local auth setup.

prompt_templates.title: Plan End-to-End Route Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the route-tester skill to plan route tests for [feature]. Include authenticated calls, failure cases, and database verification steps.

output_examples.input: Test a protected workflow start route locally.
output_examples.output: A concise checklist with the full local URL, authentication method, expected status, and database table to verify.

output_examples.input: A protected endpoint returns 403 during local testing.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting sequence covering user role, mock auth headers, route permissions, and service logs.

output_examples.input: Verify a file upload route after a code change.
output_examples.output: A local test plan covering token generation, upload request fields, expected response, and storage verification.

best_practices: Use mock authentication only in isolated development or test environments.
Regenerate local test tokens before debugging expired-cookie failures.
Verify database changes only against local or disposable test data.
anti_patterns: Do not copy mock authentication settings into production configuration.
Do not reuse documented test passwords for shared or deployed services.
Do not run database commands before confirming the target environment.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command patterns and troubleshooting steps for local route testing.

faq.question: Which authentication style does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes cookie-based JWT authentication using a refresh token cookie.

faq.question: Can it help with mock authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents mock auth variables and headers for development and test use.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production testing?
faq.answer: No. The examples target local services and development-only authentication behavior.

faq.question: Does it support database verification?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for checking local database records after route changes.

faq.question: What tools must already exist?
faq.answer: The project must provide the helper script, local services, middleware, and database container.
